expectations.text: Correctly applies the CS-coefficient thresholds (0.25 minimum, 0.5 acceptable)
expectations.evidence: "CS ≥ 0.50 is good, ≥ 0.25 is the floor for any interpretation at all, < 0.25 means the ordering collapses when you drop a modest fraction of your sample." The table also explicitly marks the 0.25 threshold and uses ≥0.25 and ≥0.50 as decision criteria for each index.

expectations.text: Concludes that Closeness and Betweenness should not be interpreted given the CS values
expectations.evidence: "Closeness and Betweenness should be dropped from your writeup" and the table assigns both a verdict of "Do not interpret" given CS = 0.13 and CS = 0.05 respectively, both below the 0.25 floor.

expectations.text: Concludes that Strength and Expected Influence are interpretable but with caution
expectations.evidence: Strength is labeled "Report with caveats" (CS = 0.36) and Expected Influence "Report with moderate confidence" (CS = 0.44). The writeup explicitly says "Strength (CS = 0.36) is interpretable but sits in the lower half of the acceptable range" and provides hedged language for Expected Influence.

expectations.text: Recommends focusing on edge ordering rather than absolute edge values when CIs are wide
expectations.evidence: "Don't interpret specific edge values as precise estimates... exact magnitudes shouldn't be the focus" and "The graph structure (which edges are present/absent) is generally more stable than edge magnitudes. Focus your substantive interpretation there."

expectations.text: Recommends the bootstrapped difference test before making specific edge or node comparisons
expectations.evidence: "Use the bootstrapped difference test for edges before claiming any two specific edges differ in strength" and "use the bootstrapped difference tests (the differenceTest() output) to identify which pairwise centrality comparisons are actually distinguishable."
